text: You're in a queue, just trying to get through. The familiar frustration starts: this line feels incredibly slow. You just want to reach the front.
Then you glance over. The other lines? They're flying! People are zipping past. It feels like everyone else is moving, while you're stuck still.
You start to wonder: is it just you? Does every queue you choose become the slowest? Is some unseen force targeting your line?
Here’s the invisible system: it's your memory playing tricks. When your line moves fast, you barely notice. When it’s slow, you’re stuck, confirming your bad luck.
The lines you *don't* join, you only see them fast. You don't observe them when stalled, because you aren't there.
This memory bias makes you feel like you're always losing. But now you know: it's not bad luck, just how your brain processes the wait.
